newsitem.title: USA: Dow asks judge to stay order allowing Louisiana trial.
newsitem.headline: Dow asks judge to stay order allowing Louisiana trial.

text.p: Attorneys for Dow Chemical Co. Thursday asked a federal judge in Michigan to stay her order that would allow part of a Louisiana breast implant lawsuit to proceed.

The attorneys filed a motion asking U.S. District Judge Denise Page Hood to forestall the effect of her order until the company can ask the U.S. Appeals Court for the Sixth Circuit to review the ruling, Dow Chemical said in a news release.
On Wednesday, Hood granted an emergency request by plaintiffs in the Louisiana case to allow a two-month old trial to proceed.

Dow Chemical and its joint venture with Corning Inc., Dow Corning Corp., argue that Hood's ruling does not conform with the Sixth Circuit's May 8 direction to consolidate and expedite the litigation, and should be reversed.
An attorney for the plaintiff's in Louisiana said the move by Dow was expected.

The trial -- one of the first class action suits to go to trial against the Midland, Mich.-based chemical giant -- had been halted earlier this month by an appeals court ruling that consolidated all breast implant cases against Dow Chemical and Corning in the Eastern District of Michigan.

The first phase of the four-phase trial began jury selection March 17 in Louisiana Civil District in New Orleans before Judge Yada Magee. The trial has generated 5,000 pages of testimony and arguments and about 300 exhibits.

Hood's order applies to the first two phases of the trial. During those parts, jurors must determine if Dow Chemical bears responsibility for alleged injuries of eight of the 1,813 class members because of its silicone testing.

Dow Chemical admits it tested silicone for Dow Corning, but denies the tests were for silicone gel breast implants. The companies each own 50 percent of Dow Corning, at one time the world's largest maker of silicone gel breast implants.
In a May 8 decision, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that all state and federal implant suits against Dow Chemical and Corning should be consolidated in federal court in Detroit.
Dow Corning is operating under bankruptcy court protection. Thousands of breast implant cases filed against it have already been consolidated in Michigan federal court.
Women with the breast implants have alleged the implants cause numerous health problems, including lupus and rheumatoid arthritis.
Dow Chemical's stock fell 37.5 cents to $84.375, while Corning slid 12.5 cents to $49.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
